summary.intent: Add automated validation to the wisp-plugins repo: a cross-reference checker for plugin/agent/skill references in docs, and a platform-limits checker with tests, wired into the justfile and CI.
summary.outcome: Prototyped a cross-reference scan that found only 6 unresolved references, then wrote scripts/check-platform-limits.py with unit tests, fixed an issue in it, and wired it into the justfile and validate.yml; the final `just check` run was issued but its result isn't shown in the transcript.

repo: Repo layout: plugins/<name>/{README.md,agents/*.md,skills/*/SKILL.md}, plus harnesses/codex/plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md, and top-level docs README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/pipeline-walkthrough.md.
Docs reference plugin components in two styles: `plugin:name` (colon) and `plugin/name` (slash); a regex scan checks these against actual agent filenames and skill directory names.

Unresolved references flagged by the scan involve navigator (estimate, challenge), ranger (scan, verify), and muse (draft, audit) READMEs, which were then inspected against the agents/skills directories.
Work is happening in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/frontend-design-evaluation.
Validation is run via `just check`, with a parallel CI job in .github/workflows/validate.yml; tests use unittest under tests/ (e.g. tests.test_platform_limits).
workflow: Prototype analysis scripts in a file rather than inline heredocs when the command guard rejects long inline scripts.
Run a prototype scan first to gauge signal-to-noise before committing to building a permanent check.
Add new checks with unit tests, then wire them into both the local justfile and CI so they run in both places.

friction: The command guard intermittently rejected long inline python heredocs, forcing the prototype into a file.
The first run of the new test suite required a follow-up edit to check-platform-limits.py, suggesting an initial bug or test mismatch.
open_items: The 6 unresolved navigator/ranger/muse references were examined but the transcript doesn't show whether they were fixed or allowlisted.
The cross-reference prototype (proto_xref.py) lives in a temp jobs directory and wasn't shown being promoted into a permanent repo check.
The result of the final `just check` run is not shown, so full-pipeline success is unconfirmed.
